page: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture running at 3.3 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio and no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, includes 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and does not feature local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in memory and processing tasks. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, software compilation with Clang, and text and image processing. Its memory subsystem demonstrates high read-only bandwidth, scoring in the top tier for Passmark memory and database operations, alongside 136.27 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, write bandwidth for large uncached blocks and single-core stress-ng performance fall into the average category.

The resource configuration and performance profile make this instance suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. The dedicated physical core design ensures consistent compute performance without resource sharing, though the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage for persistent data. The ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for compatible software stacks, though workloads requiring x86-specific instruction sets or GPU acceleration are not supported.
